title: Luca Pelizzari
text:
My name is Luca Pelizzari and I am a postdoctoral researcher in applied mathematics in the group of Christa Cuchiero at the University of Vienna. I obtained my PhD under the supervision of Christian Bayer and Peter Friz at WIAS/TU Berlin.


My research develops mathematical foundations for stochastic models with memory, with applications to mathematical finance and machine learning. I am particularly interested in rough paths and signatures, stochastic Volterra equations, stochastic volatility models, and learning methods for non-Markovian data.

title: Research
text: My research lies at the intersection of stochastic analysis, rough paths, Volterra equations, mathematical finance, and machine learning on path space.

title: Research
text:
Themes

Volterra signatures
I study signature-type transforms for Volterra paths and non-Markovian systems, with applications to universality, kernel methods, and learning on path space.


Rough volatility and affine Volterra processes
I am interested in rough volatility models, affine Volterra processes, and the analytic and numerical structures behind them.


Signatures and machine learning
I work on signature-based and kernel-based methods for regression, classification, and path-dependent data analysis.

title: Code
text:
Code accompanying my research papers and numerical experiments can be found on   GitHub .




Stochastic control with expected signatures

  Repository 

Implementation of the expected signature formula via coordinate change. An illustration solving the optimal tracking of fractional Brownian motion is presented.




Time-series learning with Volterra signatures

  Repository 

Regression and classification experiments with real-world data and time-series features built from the Volterra signature. The code relies on the JAX-based Python package tensordev, see  tensordev, which implements algorithms from the accompanying technical paper on computational aspects of the Volterra signature.




Rough PDEs for European options and Greeks

  Repository 

Code for pricing European options and computing Greeks in general local stochastic volatility models via a finite-difference implementation of the rough PDE pricing method.




Optimal stopping with signatures

  Repository 

Implementation of primal and dual algorithms for solving non-Markovian optimal stopping problems with path signatures. The examples include stopping problems for fractional Brownian motion, American option pricing under rough-volatility models such as rough Bergomi and rough Heston, and extensions to deep and kernel learning.




Local regression with signatures

  Repository 

Local kernel regression and classification on path space using signature-based distances. The repository contains implementations for path-valued regression and classification tasks, including examples for time series, SDE learning, and path-dependent option pricing.

title: Code
text:
Examples



tensordev: Volterra signatures

  Repository 

tensordev is a JAX-based Python package for tensor algebra, signatures, free developments, Volterra signatures, and related kernel computations.
It provides numerical routines for working with signature-type objects and is used in computational experiments involving Volterra signatures and Volterra signature kernels.
Related experiments for learning with Volterra signatures can be found here:
  Volterra signature learning 




Rough PDEs for European options and Greeks

  Repository 

Code for partial Monte Carlo pricing and Greek computation for European options via sample-wise rough PDEs.
The repository contains finite-difference routines for solving the pathwise PDEs, computing prices and Greeks, and simulating rough-volatility input paths.




Optimal stopping with signatures

  Repository 

Code for primal and dual methods for non-Markovian optimal stopping using path signatures.
The examples include stopping problems for fractional Brownian motion and American option pricing under rough-volatility models such as rough Bergomi and rough Heston.




Local regression with signatures

  Repository 

Code for Nadaraya-Watson regression and classification on path space using signature-based distances.
The repository contains implementations for path-valued regression and classification tasks, including examples for time series, SDE learning, and path-dependent option pricing.
